summary: Free project-based course on the files, state, checks and controls that make AI coding agents work reliably on real projects.

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: Learn Harness Engineering is a course about the 'harness' around a coding agent: its instructions, tools, environment, state and feedback. Lectures explain the ideas, hands-on projects apply them to the same Electron knowledge-base app, and a resource library provides copy-ready templates such as AGENTS.md, feature_list.json and init.sh.
sixtySeconds.problem: A smart model still fails on real projects without structure. The course teaches how to give agents a clear manual, progress tracking and verification so their work holds up.
whoFor: Developers using Claude Code, Codex or other coding agents
Teams adopting agents on real codebases
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for practical, agent-agnostic methods you can apply today with ready templates, plus deeper lectures and projects.
requirements: A coding agent and a project to try the templates on

overview: Start right away: drop the starter files into your repo, an AGENTS.md (or CLAUDE.md) operating manual, an init.sh that installs, verifies and starts, a feature_list.json and a progress log, so each session knows what to do and what's done.
The full course has lectures (14 in the current syllabus) and hands-on projects (8) on the same capstone app, plus breakdowns of frontier harness designs.
Materials are on the documentation website and as PDF coursebooks. It is MIT licensed.
limitations: Templates need adapting to your project
